reason: The text demonstrates that the Israelite people explicitly complain to Moses and Aaron about water, food, and conditions in the wilderness (e.g., 'וַיִּלּ֜וֹנוּ כָּל־ עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל' - the whole congregation complained). Critically, these complaints are not condemned. Instead, God explicitly acknowledges them ('שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶת־ תְּלוּנֹּת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒' - 'I have heard the complaints of the children of Israel') and responds by providing manna, water, and other provisions. The narrative shows Moses and Aaron facilitating the people's needs, not suppressing complaints. The moral concerns faith in God's provision and leadership's mediation with the divine, not a prohibition on complaining.
